text:
alex: quick postmortem from the host-side profiler run — saw a p99 jump after the kernel-selector change + the new minibatcher heuristic landed. can we triage?

maria: saw that on the dashboard too. p50 fine, but p99 ~+12ms on text-stream endpoints.

alex: attaching the short perf dump i grabbed from canary (summary):
```
route: /v1/stream/generate
model: gpt-large-8k-quant
canary nodes: 3
p50: 18ms -> 18ms
p95: 42ms -> 45ms
p99: 78ms -> 90ms
throughput: -5%
CPU host parse: +18%
KV cache hit rate: 94% -> 88%
```

jin: interesting — KV hit droppage stands out. did kernel selection cause different shard alignment or header size changes?

sam: i instrumented the tokenizer edge: the new kernel path reduced decode cycles on GPU, but host preparse now emits slightly larger framing for small streaming writes (more microchunks). that increases syscalls and increases parse overhead.

maria: can you paste the token-framing snippet?

sam: sure — from the preparse shim:
```
// old: coalesce until >= 512 bytes or timeout
if (buffered >= 512) flush();
// new: minibatcher tries to keep batches small for latency-sensitive sequences
if (tokens_count >= minibatch_hint) flush();
```

sam: minibatch_hint defaults to 6 which for short prompts causes ~3-4 small writes instead of 1.

alex: that explains syscall spike. perf top on host showed sys_read/sys_write and parse_tokenizer hot.

perf-bot: 1751239999 - rule: host_cpu > 10% increase, alert created: #1751

jin: KV cache drop might be secondary: more fragmented frames -> different key prefixes for streaming cache lookup TTLs. we saw evictions earlier in the day.

maria: got a small flamegraph — attaching inline:
```
host_cpu:
  parse_stream (40%)
  sys_write (18%)
  kvcache.lookup (12%)
  grpc_unary (8%)
```

alex: hypothesis: kernel change reduced GPU time but shifted work to host because minibatcher heuristic encouraged smaller outbound chunks. combo -> p99 regression.

sam: quick experiment idea: revert minibatcher hint to 24 on canary, keep kernel change. see delta.

jin: also try enabling coalesce-bytes threshold at 512 regardless of minibatch_hint for streaming routes.

maria: i'll roll a canary with both tweaks in 10 mins. will monitor p99 and kv hit.

perf-bot: canary 1751240005 started (nodes=3). health ok.

alex: thanks. if that fixes p99 we can do a better follow-up: adjust kernel selector to prefer paths that don't alter host framing, or make minibatcher heuristics framing-aware.

sam: also worth adding a small kvcache probe to detect fragmentation and adjust TTLs dynamically.

maria: quick update after 6 mins: p99 back to 80ms, KV hit 93%, CPU parse down ~10%. trending stable.

jin: good signal. next actions: 1) revert/minor-tune minibatcher default for streaming routes 2) add kernel-selection test that vets framing output on host 3) add kvcache fragmentation telemetry 4) write a microbenchmark for small write counts.

alex: will create GH issue list from this thread. thanks y'all. :thumbsup:

sam: can we also add a quick test in CI that runs a short-end-to-end with short prompts and asserts coalesced_writes <= 2 for typical cases?

alex: yes — add to runtime-integration -> e2e-tokenization smoke.

maria: noted. closing triage when GH issues are up.

perf-bot: 1751240088 - canary tracker: pass -> promote candidate if no regressions in 30m.
